name: Moss Icon
lede: Moss Icon were mostly high schoolers in Annapolis when they started in 1986, and barely played outside Maryland and DC. Their one LP came out two years after they split, and has been filed among emo's forebears ever since.

facts.h: Most of them were in high school when it started
facts.p: By the time their only LP came out, Bandcamp Daily notes, they were just into their early 20s.

src.title: Moss Icon Were One of a Kind (Bandcamp Daily)

facts.h: They broke up and got back together "four or five or six times"
facts.p: That's guitarist Tonie Joy on 1987 to 1991; he calls the band "pretty dysfunctional." Lyburnum Wits End Liberation Fly came out in 1993, two years after the last breakup.

src.title: Moss Icon Were One of a Kind (Bandcamp Daily)

facts.h: The reissue label's owner met Joy in a Baltimore post office
facts.p: Years later, Jeremy deVine's Temporary Residence put out the 30th-anniversary reissue of Lyburnum, remastered by Alan Douches.
